macro.narrative: Thursday's violent reversal was a political-risk shock to AI capex, not fresh macro data: markets re-read Tuesday's Democratic sweep overnight as a threat to the AI data-center buildout after Texas's governor-elect campaigned on pausing new construction in the largest US data-center market, with UBS flagging up to a third of projected 2028 capacity at risk. That hit debt-financed GPU buyers (CoreWeave -14.3%) atop credit spreads already at a 17-month high on AI-debt-binge fears (HY yields +~90bp to ~7%, spreads +94bp to 354bp); crucially, AMD beat and raised guidance yet still fell ~15%, confirming sentiment/policy rather than fundamentals drove the move. Hawkish Fed speak (Hammack: rates need to go restrictive; Musalem: a hike is needed soon) removed the rate-cut cushion, and CME-implied odds now sit near 68-73% for a December hike. $2.5T was erased from the Nasdaq in one session; NYSE breadth was roughly 6:1 negative. Oil, meanwhile, round-tripped the other way: Wednesday's Iran-de-escalation-driven crash reversed Thursday (Brent proxy +4.9% to ~$99.25) as Iran's IRGC reportedly set tankers/a tug ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz (five incidents since Sunday, matching October's record pace) and Saudi Arabia warned of fresh Houthi threats to the Yanbu Red Sea hub. Gold held its post-election bid (GLD +0.8%) while silver and the miners sold off harder (SLV -0.5%, SILJ -1.6%, HL -3.3%, PAAS -2.2%) -- Kitco's PM wrap attributes this to silver's dual industrial-metal exposure amplifying beta to the tech-led equity rout, not a silver-specific catalyst (no COMEX margin change, no SLV outflow). Today's Oct NFP (consensus 65K vs Sept's 29K miss, unemployment steady at 4.2%) is the swing variable: a soft print could revive rate-cut hope and lift riskOnProb back toward 0.5; a hot print into an already-hawkish Fed could push it toward 0.2. A fourth possible government shutdown looms too, with the CR expiring Dec 11 and Congress returning Nov 9 for a lame-duck session with no appropriations progress.

rareEarthCalls.name: JL Mag Rare-Earth Co
drivers: JL Mag is mainland China's largest NdFeB magnet producer, making it the direct read-through for Beijing's rare-earth export-control policy rather than a 'China+1' ex-China beneficiary like Lynas/MP
